headline.title: Two shocks hit over the weekend, and they push opposite ways. U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz; Iran answered with missiles on two U.S. bases in Jordan, and the White House threatened Kharg Island, the terminal that moves ~90% of Iran's crude. Brent is back above $90, WTI in the mid-$80s. Energy is the one green sector on the board: USO +3.4%, HAL +2.6%, COP +2.5%, CVX +2.3%, OXY +2.2%, XOM +2.1%.
headline.summary: The second shock is monetary and it is the bigger one. In his first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair, Warsh went hawkish — "the Fed's predominant focus right now should be on prices" — with headline PCE 3.7% and core 3.3%. September rate-hike odds jumped to ~57% from ~35%, the short end popped ~8bp in a bear flattener. A hike is now the live debate, which makes Friday's payrolls the highest-stakes print of the quarter. Oil spiking into a Fed already worried about prices is the uncomfortable part. Separately, California utilities are in a second day of collapse: PCG −17.1% after −16.6% Friday on 114.4M shares, EIX −15.9%, SRE −3.6%, all cut by Mizuho.

overview: Month-end with a quiet U.S. docket, so oil and the Warsh repricing set the tone. Friday's Strat board has a Failed 2U cluster on the index itself — SPY, QQQ and VOO all broke Thursday's high and closed back under it — with AVGO and SNOW failing the same way into Wednesday earnings. Against that, dark pool was index accumulation: VOO $3.1B and SPY $2.5B cumulative, all ask-side. The signal and the flow disagree, which is the day's real tension. The 9/4 straddle prices AVGO at an 8.1% move, twice NVDA's 3.8%, and a $2.5M AVGO $370C 9/4 sweep already sits on top of it. SNDK, CRS and ATI join the MSCI World Index at the close.
setups: The cleanest convergence on the board: a Failed 2D with clustering on Friday's candle, and a real overnight catalyst underneath it. Hormuz strikes put Brent over $90. XOM also showed up in the ≤3-print concentrated-interest group — a few large tickets, not a drip.

Friday took Thursday's 772.355 high to 775.30 and closed 769.35, back below it. The low never broke, so this is a failed upside break, not an outside day. QQQ and VOO printed the identical failure. Three index vehicles failing the same level on the same day is the strongest Strat signal on the board.

Failed 2U with clustering, reports Wednesday, the 9/4 straddle prices an 8.1% move — the highest on the board — and the largest sweep on either board was $2.5M of AVGO $370C expiring 9/4, sitting right on the print. Signal, vol and flow all pointing at one name.

darkpool.note: Friday leaned ask-side across mega-cap single prints — with NVDA the exception. The biggest single-name print was GOOGL $708M ask-side, but NVDA topped cumulative single-name flow at $2.3B bid-side, #1 on the entire board ex-ETFs, ahead of GOOGL $1.3B ask and AAPL $939M bid. On the ETF side it was pure index accumulation, all ask: VOO $3.1B and SPY $2.5B cumulative — the two biggest lines on the whole board. That is the day's central conflict: the Strat board has SPY, QQQ and VOO all printing Failed 2U, while the flow shows institutions buying those exact vehicles into the close. Outsized-for-cap prints: VEEV $43.3M on a ~$28B cap with a 3.4x flow surge, and ENTG $32.5M on ~$18B with 5.5x.
